curation.notes: Synthetic (non-biological) chemomechanical system: directional base-triggered disassembly of VsA amphiphile microcrystalline fibres pulls adsorbed polystyrene microspheres; force measured with a LUMICKS C-Trap in dual-trap mode (stall force 2.3 pN). Not single-molecule in the strict sense (bead-fibre multivalent contact). AFM colloidal-probe adhesion spectroscopy in air is a secondary force measurement; Raman, XRD, GIWAXS, cryo-EM are characterisation only.

evidence.snippet: The force was measured by a position-sensitive detector in two dimensions on both beads with an acquisition rate of 78 kHz.
To analyse and store the force-trace data, the force acquisition frequency was downsampled to 150 Hz using the pylake Python package47.
The force resolution of this calibration was estimated to be 100.0 fN at 150 Hz, with a theoretical limit of 0.4 fN for a typical trap stiffness of 16.5 fN nm–1 at room temperature.
The force spectroscopy measurements were carried out using NH3-functionalized polystyrene microspherical probes (diameter, d = 1.0 μm) with spring constant k = 0.03 N m–1 (PT.PS.NH3, Novascan).

entities.name: VsA amphiphile microcrystalline fibres (coumarin-based pH switch)

evidence.snippet: An amphiphilic monomer self-assembles into rigid, high-aspect-ratio microcrystalline fibres. The assembly process is regulated by a coumarin-based pH switching motif.

source.snippet: quantifying a stall force of 2.3 pN (±0.1 pN) exerted by the ratcheting mechanism produced by the disassembly of the microfibres.
